The series was serialized in the magazine Monthly Shōnen Gangan from 2003 to 2007 and collected into nine tankōbon volumes by Square Enix.

Meaning is not found in The Record of a Fallen Vampire — it is manufactured for it. It was licensed in English by Viz Media, which released the volumes from May 2008 and May 2010. A sequel manga titled Vampire Jūji-Kai: Inu ni wa Inu no Uta began serialization in Monthly Shōnen Gangan in October 2026.

The cold light on The Record of a Fallen Vampire leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. An anime television series adaptation produced by Zero-G and Liber is set to premiere in 2027. The story follows Strauss, a former vampire king, as he searches for his queen Adelheid, who was sealed away one thousand years earlier.

The Record of a Fallen Vampire did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. His quest draws the attention of dhampirs, humans, and the supernatural force known as the Black Swan. The honest version of The Record of a Fallen Vampire starts by giving up the comforting part. While the other dhampires believe his motive is a deep love for his queen, Bridget believes that Strauss wants to find Adelheid so he can personally kill her as revenge for killing Stella. He is also unusually cool and logical which allows him to master both the politics and the art of war with frightening precision.

Strip The Record of a Fallen Vampire of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Strauss was seen by many as a god and thus great things were expected of him. Few ever stopped to think about his personal life as he devoted himself to his duties as general and later king.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — The Record of a Fallen Vampire shows exactly where that breaks. The many mysteries in the series revolve around him and the mysterious fall of his kingdom 1000 years ago. All attempts to pry information from him failed, and he resents the attempts to bring up the unhappy past.

What looks like free choice in The Record of a Fallen Vampire is older than choice itself. Before becoming king, Strauss was a general of the Kingdom of the Night. He was also in love with a human girl, Stella, whom he presented with a pendant made from lunar rock which he collected himself.

Nobody designed the part of The Record of a Fallen Vampire you experience — it was inherited. Later it is revealed that Strauss never loved Adelheid, and that his true love interest was only Stella. As the general, Strauss had never been defeated on the field of battle; because of his exceptional leadership of the armies, the Kingdom of Night went without a loss for over 100 years.

Every serious account of The Record of a Fallen Vampire eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. While he was a general, Strauss had the cunning and power to be able to control the entire continent. He also knew that if he conquered more, the people will hate the Kingdom and rebel, causing the loss of many lives, which would be unacceptable.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of The Record of a Fallen Vampire — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. Nevertheless, he chooses to limit his power and fight in close combat in order to avoid damage to the surroundings. He is usually seen fighting with a vibrating edge of magic, although he can also summon a sword and is an expert swordsman.

The selfish-gene reading of The Record of a Fallen Vampire makes it less romantic and far more precise. At range, Strauss can cast vibrating magic arrows or destroy missiles with a single gesture of his hand. Although pure-blooded vampires perish when exposed to sunlight, Strauss has overcome this limitation long ago.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. Despite being extremely powerful, Strauss is very kind-hearted, gentle, and has compassion for everyone except himself. It is later revealed that he abandoned his kingdom and turned himself into the ultimate enemy so both human and vampire races will collaborate and stop fighting each other, continuing to carry everyone's resentment for him for over 1000 years to protect everyone.

The feeling that The Record of a Fallen Vampire means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Strauss' queen and Bridget's half-sister, Adelheid was sealed a thousand years ago when she went berserk and unleashed her power, the Moonlight of Corrosion (腐食の月, Fushoku no Gekkou). Though unskilled in the use of her magic, Adelheid is potentially more powerful than Strauss and her magic possesses terraforming capabilities; the corrosive nature of her powers resulted from unleashing it all at once and she, like Strauss, is not limited by exposure to sunlight.

Nothing in The Record of a Fallen Vampire was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Legend says that she went berserk when she thought that the king had been killed, though Bridget believes that Adelheid was frightened and thought Strauss was going to kill her when he believed Adelheid had killed Stella and her unborn child. Nobody knew that she had witnessed Stella's death until Adelheid officially became Strauss' queen.

The psychology underneath The Record of a Fallen Vampire is simpler and older than the story on top. Adelheid had a shy and self-conscious personality and she always worried about how others thought of her. Unlike Bridget or Strauss, Adelheid does not possess an exceptional amount of brains or cunning.

Behind The Record of a Fallen Vampire sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. By comparison, Adelheid was the least skilled of the three but since she was the only pure-blooded daughter of the king, Adelheid was the only one who could become queen. When Adelheid first learned that Bridget was her sister, the future queen felt very guilty over the circumstances of her birth.

The nihilist does not deny The Record of a Fallen Vampire — he only refuses to flatter it. Adelheid always tried to make it up to Bridget by calling the dhampire 'dear sister' and she and Bridget became close. After she is reawakened, she strives to atone for her weakness and past mistakes, particularly in regards to Stella's death, the deterioration of the Kingdom of the Night, and Strauss' downfall.

What culture calls destiny in The Record of a Fallen Vampire is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Like most rulers of the Kingdom of the Night, he became king at the age of 1000. Gottfried is an intelligent man that commanded the nation for several hundred years.

The genes do not care about The Record of a Fallen Vampire; they care about copies. Thus, when Bridget was born, she was allowed to be princess and heir in the off chance that Gottfried died. As soon as Adelheid was born, Gottfried banished his older daughter in order to prevent civil war between the two children.

Take away the meaning and The Record of a Fallen Vampire still functions — that is the disturbing part. Those who have both vampire and human blood are referred to as dhampires. All dhampires, except Laetitia, have united under Bridget against Strauss and his quest for the seal.

The unconscious does not argue with The Record of a Fallen Vampire; it simply acts first. Bridget is the leader of the dhampire community, a highly capable and powerful dhamphir who has been fighting Strauss for over a thousand years. Bridget has set up thousands of 'nets' all over the world that allows her to track the activities of Strauss and she is highly organized and efficient.

The Record of a Fallen Vampire feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. In battle, Bridget acts as the strategist, directing the other dhampires' attacks. Bridget was adopted by Strauss when he was still a general, and raised like his own daughter; he was personally responsible for cultivating Bridget's abilities.

The bleak reading of The Record of a Fallen Vampire is also the most testable one. According to Tessenji, Bridget's skill in the area of politics as well as her abilities with a sword, is the only reason that the dhampire survived after Strauss abdicated. Bridget is an expert in small group combat, and she has a keen military intelligence and excellent political sense.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about The Record of a Fallen Vampire. Despite the fact that she was only 150 and was a dhampire, she later served as one of his most trusted generals. Despite her history with Strauss, Bridget keeps her personal feelings and that of the dhampire community separate.

The self that experiences The Record of a Fallen Vampire is a committee, not a king. There are several instances where Bridget allows herself to feel angry that she is not helping Strauss. While serving the Kingdom of the Night, the only thing that separated her from becoming Strauss' lover is the family-like status they had.

Reproduction explains more of The Record of a Fallen Vampire than any philosophy dares to admit.
